title: Build Larger Systems From Smaller Objects
content:
What problem does this solve?
A useful program eventually becomes too large for one object to own every detail. Composition builds a larger object from smaller objects with clearer responsibilities. A Character can have Equipment. A Party can have Character objects.

Model has-a relationships
If one concept naturally contains or collaborates with another, storing the smaller object as an attribute often keeps related state and behavior together.

Do not duplicate component state
If Equipment already owns weapon and armor, Character can store an Equipment object rather than copying weapon and armor fields onto itself. The larger object can ask its component for information.

Keep reference choices explicit
A Party may copy the outer member list so later changes to the caller's list do not change membership accidentally, while still intentionally containing references to the Character objects themselves. Separate characters should receive separate Equipment objects when independence is required.

Vocabulary after the behavior
Composition is building one object from other objects. A component is an object contained by a larger object. Responsibility describes which object should own a piece of state or behavior.
concepts: Composition models has-a relationships by storing objects inside other objects
Components keep their own related state/behavior instead of duplicating fields on the parent
A collection object can contain several existing objects
Responsibility decisions matter more than simply creating more classes
Reference independence still matters when composing mutable components

examples.title: One object has another
examples.explanation: Car contains an Engine object and reads state through that component.

examples.title: Collection of objects
examples.explanation: The Team stores a separate outer list that contains references to the member objects.

common_mistakes: Duplicating component fields directly on a parent instead of storing the component object
Putting all state and behavior in one giant Character class
Accidentally giving independent owners the same mutable component
Creating classes without a meaningful responsibility boundary
Introducing inheritance or other new syntax in the integration capstone

exercises.title: Spot the has-a relationship
exercises.prompt: A Car has an Engine. Is composition a natural model for this relationship?
choices: Yes; Car can contain an Engine component.
No; every engine field must be copied directly onto Car.
hints: Say the relationship aloud: a Car has an Engine.
That language suggests one object can contain another object with its own responsibility.
Composition is a natural fit.

exercises.title: Read through a component
hints: car.engine first retrieves the contained Engine object.
The next `.power` reads the attribute from that component.
The output is 100.

exercises.title: Store a component
exercises.prompt: Complete Character so its constructor stores the supplied equipment object in `self.equipment`.
hints: The equipment object is already provided as a constructor parameter.
Composition here only requires storing that object on this Character.
Assign `self.equipment = equipment`.

exercises.title: Two separate components
exercises.prompt: Aria receives one `Equipment("spear")` instance and Rook receives a separate `Equipment("axe")` instance. If `aria.equipment.weapon` changes to `"bow"`, who should be affected?
hints: The two Equipment objects were constructed separately.
Changing an attribute on one component changes that component only.
Only Aria is affected.

exercises.title: Contain a component?
exercises.prompt: Character has equipment with several related fields/behaviors. Which design keeps responsibility clearer?
choices: Store an Equipment object on Character and let Equipment manage equipment-related state.
Duplicate every equipment field directly on Character.
hints: Avoid duplicating one concept's state in two places.
The equipment data belongs together as its own component.
Store the Equipment object on Character.

exercises.title: Shared component by accident
exercises.prompt: Both heroes were given the same Equipment instance, but the requirement says independent equipment. Repair only the construction code so each receives its own Equipment object.
hints: The class definitions are already fine; inspect which object is passed to both Character calls.
One `gear` object is currently reused twice. Construct a new Equipment for each character.
Call `Equipment("sword")` separately for Aria and Rook.

exercises.title: Equipment component
exercises.prompt: Define `Equipment(weapon, armor)` and a `summary()` method returning exactly `{"weapon": ..., "armor": ...}`.
hints: Use __init__ to store both constructor inputs on the instance.
summary reads those attributes and returns one dictionary; it does not need to mutate anything.
Store self.weapon/self.armor, then return both named fields from summary.

exercises.title: Character contains equipment
exercises.prompt: Define `Character(name, health, equipment)` storing the supplied Equipment object. Add `summary()` returning exactly `name`, `health`, and `equipment`, where the equipment value is `self.equipment.summary()`. Include or reuse a working Equipment class in your solution.
hints: Character should store the Equipment object itself, not duplicate weapon/armor fields.
In summary, delegate equipment formatting to the component's summary method.
Return name, health, and `self.equipment.summary()` in one dictionary.

exercises.title: Party contains characters
exercises.prompt: A small Character class is supplied for testing. Define `Party(members)` so it stores `list(members)` as a separate outer list. Add `total_health()` summing every `member.health` without `sum()`, and `names()` returning a list of every `member.name`. Do not copy the Character objects themselves.
hints: Copy only the outer members list in __init__; the contained Character objects remain the members.
total_health needs a normal accumulator loop. names needs a result list and append loop.
Use `self.members = list(members)`, then two methods that iterate self.members and return their accumulated results.

tests.message: Party must store a separate outer list so later caller-list changes do not alter party.members.

exercises.title: Expedition Model v1
exercises.prompt: Build `Equipment`, `Character`, and `Party` using composition. The supplied `build_expedition()` contains a deliberate shared-component bug: both heroes are constructed with the same Equipment object. After implementing the classes, repair the builder so it returns Aria (health 10, spear/leather) and Rook (health 14, axe/mail) with separate Equipment objects. Equipment has weapon/armor and summary(). Character has name/health/equipment and summary(). Party stores a separate outer members list; total_health(), names(), and summary() aggregate the characters. `Party.summary()` returns exactly `member_count`, `total_health`, `names`, and `equipment` (a list of each character's equipment summary). No inheritance or comprehensions.
hints: Build and verify each layer separately: Equipment first, then Character storing Equipment, then Party storing Characters.
Party aggregation should delegate/read through its contained Character objects rather than duplicate their state. Use ordinary loops, not comprehensions.

Repair the supplied shared `gear` construction: create spear/leather equipment for Aria and axe/mail equipment for Rook as separate objects. Hidden checks verify identity, aggregation, caller-list isolation, and an empty Party.

tests.message: Party must copy only the outer members list so caller-list appends do not change the party.

exercises.success_message: Beginner-core capstone complete: smaller objects own coherent responsibilities, the Party aggregates them, and mutable components are independent where the model requires independence.
